styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, colonial plazas and the city's art scene.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Arepas, street grills and long lunches in Las Mercedes.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: El Ávila mountain views and green escapes above the city.

stays.why: Central, walkable and close to the metro; good base for museums and plazas. Check the exact rate on the day.
Best for food and nightlife; many restaurants and bars within walking distance.
Cheapest of the four and near the main museums and parks; busier and less polished at night.
Quiet, leafy streets with cafés and offices; a calm base between Altamira and Las Mercedes.

food: Try an arepa: grilled corn bread filled with cheese, shredded beef or black beans. Cheap and everywhere.
Pabellón criollo is the national plate: shredded beef, rice, black beans and fried plantain.
Las Mercedes has the widest choice of restaurants and cafés; book ahead on weekends.
Street grills and bakeries are the cheapest meals. Prices in VES move fast, so ask before you order.
Coffee is strong and local. Order a cortadito at a café counter for a quick, cheap stop.
more_time: Ride the cable car up El Ávila (Waraira Repano) for city views and cool air; check it is running on the day.
Add a day for the colonial centre and the birthplace of Simón Bolívar, if it is open to visitors.
Food lovers can swap one museum morning for a market visit and a long lunch in Las Mercedes.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the museums, plazas and a good food evening; add a third for El Ávila or a day out.

month_notes: January: mild and fairly dry, around 12 rain days. Good for walking the city.
February: one of the driest months, about 11 rain days. Comfortable days and cool nights.
March: rain picks up to about 17 days. Carry a light rain jacket.
April: warmer nights near 19°C and 18 rain days. Plan indoor sights for afternoons.
May: mild but wetter, about 16 rain days. Mornings are usually the best window.
June: around 20 rain days. Expect short heavy showers; keep plans flexible.
July: the wettest stretch begins, about 24 rain days. Pack a rain layer.
August: wettest month, about 25 rain days. El Ávila trails may be muddy; check on the day.
September: still wet, around 20 rain days. Similar to June.
October: about 22 rain days. Showers common; evenings stay mild.
November: cooler highs near 26°C and 22 rain days. Bring a layer for evenings.
December: cooler nights near 18°C and 17 rain days. Pleasant for city walks.

climate_guide.summary: Mild all year at this altitude: highs around 26–28°C, cool nights, and rain in every month. The driest months are January and February.

items.title: Mild all year
items.text: Highs stay around 26–28°C and lows around 17–20°C. No extreme heat or cold.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect 11–25 rain days a month. Showers are often short; a light rain jacket helps.

items.title: Wettest: July and August
items.text: About 24–25 rain days. Keep indoor options ready and check mountain trips on the day.

items.title: Driest: January and February
items.text: Around 11–12 rain days. The best window for walking and outdoor plans.

items.title: Cool evenings
items.text: Nights drop to 17–20°C. Bring a light layer for evenings out.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a rain jacket or compact umbrella, and comfortable shoes for hilly streets.

transit.best: Metro for most cross-city trips; agree taxi prices first or use a ride app.

modes.text: Clean, cheap and fast. Buy a single, round trip or 10-journey multi abono.
Metrobuses link metro stations to areas off the underground, but run roughly every 20 minutes. Por puesto minibuses are cheap but slow, crowded and often in poor condition.
Taxis have no meters; agree the price first and expect quotes near double the fair fare. Uber and inDrive work but coverage varies; confirm before relying on them.
Driving is hectic. Only worth it for trips outside the city.
Fine by day in safe districts, but avoid quiet streets after dark.
